registers.name: CONTROL_0
registers.description: Software-visible control for request injection and supervisory behavior.

fields.name: REQ_ARM
fields.description: Arms software-side request submission behavior. This does not replace the streaming req_valid/req_ready interface; it only enables firmware to request that a compact request packet be prepared for transport.

fields.name: QUEUE_DEPTH_EN
fields.description: Requests the optional shallow depth-2 queue behavior when supported by the implementation parameter. If not implemented, hardware ignores the bit and reports capability accordingly.

fields.name: FALLBACK_ACK
fields.description: Firmware acknowledgement of observed fallback status; used only for status management and does not clear hardware safety state by itself.

registers.name: CONTROL_1
registers.description: Request packet software staging fields, byte 0. These fields are descriptive and compact only; they do not expose bulk payloads.

fields.name: OPCODE
fields.description: Request opcode to be packed into req_data[127:120] by firmware integration logic.

registers.name: CONTROL_2
registers.description: Request packet software staging fields, sequence low byte.

registers.name: CONTROL_3
registers.description: Request packet software staging fields, sequence high byte.

registers.name: CONTROL_4
registers.description: Request packet software staging fields, stream velocity.

fields.name: STREAM_VELOCITY
fields.description: Stream velocity metadata byte. Firmware shall encode a value within the supported 20 to 55 m/s envelope; the default reference is 38.89 m/s.

registers.name: CONTROL_5
registers.description: Request packet software staging fields, geometry metadata byte 0.

fields.name: GEOM_META_0
fields.description: Compact geometry reference metadata byte 0 identifying STL/DrivAerML reference geometry.

registers.name: CONTROL_6
registers.description: Request packet software staging fields, geometry metadata byte 1.

fields.name: GEOM_META_1
fields.description: Compact geometry reference metadata byte 1 identifying STL/DrivAerML reference geometry.

registers.name: CONTROL_7
registers.description: Request packet software staging fields, geometry metadata byte 2.

fields.name: GEOM_META_2
fields.description: Compact geometry reference metadata byte 2 identifying STL/DrivAerML reference geometry.

registers.name: CONTROL_8
registers.description: Control flags for request packet construction and transport policy.

fields.name: CTRL_FLAGS
fields.description: Control flags packed into req_data. Bits are implementation-defined within the contract and remain compact metadata only.

fields.name: REQ_VALID_SEEN

fields.name: QUEUE_OCCUPANCY

fields.name: CLAMP_STATUS

sources.name: FALLBACK_ACTIVE_IRQ
sources.description: Asserted when fallback_active becomes active due to reset, invalid packet decode, stale response, timeout, or service error.

sources.name: TIMEOUT_IRQ
sources.description: Asserted when the freshness checker reports timeout on the outstanding transaction.

sources.name: STALE_RESPONSE_IRQ
sources.description: Asserted when a response is late, mismatched, or otherwise stale and cannot drive actuators.

sources.name: CLAMP_IRQ
sources.description: Asserted when the clamp block bounds a recommendation or fallback forces conservative output.

sources.name: SERVICE_ERROR_IRQ
sources.description: Asserted when the external software/GPU service layer signals service_error.

sources.name: RESP_VALID_IRQ
sources.description: Asserted when a valid, fresh, acknowledged response is presented on the response stream.

sources.name: ACT_VALID_IRQ
sources.description: Asserted when a bounded actuator command is presented on the actuator stream.

init_sequence: Read REGMAP_ID_0..3 and VERSION_MAJOR..PATCH to confirm the expected register map.
Write CONTROL_0.REQ_ARM=0 and observe STATUS_0.FALLBACK_ACTIVE after reset until the hardware is ready.
Program request staging bytes CONTROL_1..CONTROL_8 with opcode, sequence, velocity, geometry metadata, and control flags for the next outbound transport packet.
If optional queueing is supported by the implementation, set CONTROL_0.QUEUE_DEPTH_EN only after checking firmware/bitstream capability policy.
For firmware-visible safety monitoring, read STATUS_0, STATUS_1, REQ_SEQ_OUT_0..1, and AGE_COUNTER_0..1 before issuing traffic.
polling_sequence: Poll STATUS_0 for FALLBACK_ACTIVE, TIMEOUT_SEEN, STALE_SEEN, CLAMP_SEEN, SERVICE_ERROR_SEEN, RESP_VALID_SEEN, and ACT_VALID_SEEN.
Poll STATUS_1 for STATE_CODE, ERROR_HOLD, and QUEUE_OCCUPANCY.
Poll REQ_SEQ_OUT_0..1 and AGE_COUNTER_0..1 to track the outstanding transaction and freshness age.
Poll RESP_PKT_0..5 to read echoed sequence and response status after a request completes.
Poll ACT_CMD_0..3 to observe the bounded actuator command and safe-fallback indicator.
If TIMEOUT_SEEN or STALE_SEEN is asserted, keep firmware in safety monitoring mode and submit a new request only after the condition is cleared by a valid fresh acknowledged command.
irq_sequence: On FALLBACK_ACTIVE_IRQ, stop issuing new requests, log the state code, and read STATUS_0/STATUS_1 plus ACT_CMD_0..3 for diagnostics.
On TIMEOUT_IRQ or STALE_RESPONSE_IRQ, mark the current request obsolete, read REQ_SEQ_OUT_0..1 and AGE_COUNTER_0..1, and wait for a new valid fresh acknowledged transaction.
On CLAMP_IRQ, read RESP_PKT_2 and ACT_CMD_0..3 to capture the bounded command and clamp status.
On SERVICE_ERROR_IRQ, treat the external service layer as faulted, preserve fallback, and do not clear until a subsequent valid request is accepted and acknowledged.
On RESP_VALID_IRQ and ACT_VALID_IRQ, collect RESP_PKT_0..5 and ACT_CMD_0..3 respectively for logging and traceability.

consistency_notes: All assumptions remain compatible with DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.
The register map is firmware-visible only and does not add new hardware hierarchy or ports.
The bus is described as custom because the source specification implies a compact software-visible register interface but does not mandate AXI/APB/I2C.
Any values wider than 8 bits are split across multiple byte registers.
This register map exposes compact metadata and status only; it does not expose bulk payloads, meshes, tensors, or flow fields.
